entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Louis d'Amboise (1480-1511) was a French Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal who played a pivotal role in the Council of Trent. 

As one of the most prominent clerics of his time, d'Amboise was instrumental in shaping the theological debates that led to the reform of the Catholic Church.

His contributions to the Council of Trent had far-reaching consequences, including the establishment of the Index Librorum Prohibitorum and the development of the Tridentine Mass. 

Despite his significant influence on the Church, d'Amboise's legacy is often overshadowed by that of other prominent figures from this era.

"The Lord is my shepherd, I lack nothing;
he makes me lie down in green pastures,
he leads me beside quiet waters,
he refreshes my soul." (Psalm 23:1-2)
